q: In specialization with attribute inheritance, a lower-level entity set
options: inherits all attributes and relationships of its higher-level entity set
inherits only the key of its parent and nothing else
cannot have attributes of its own
must have exactly the same number of attributes as its parent
exp: Attribute inheritance means lower-level entities automatically have the attributes (and participate in relationships) of the higher-level entity set, in addition to their own.

q: In SQL, a view is best described as
options: a physical copy of a table stored on a different disk
an index on a primary key
a virtual table defined by a stored query
exp: A view stores a query definition, not data, and presents its result as a virtual relation.

q: The theta-join R ⋈_θ S is equivalent to
exp: A theta join is a Cartesian product followed by a selection with condition θ.

q: T(a, b) = (1,10), (2,20), (3,30), (4,40). What does SELECT SUM(b) FROM T WHERE a BETWEEN 2 AND 3; return?
exp: BETWEEN is inclusive, so rows with a = 2 and 3 qualify: 20 + 30 = 50.

q: R(P, Q, R, S) has FDs PQ → R, R → S, S → P. The candidate keys are PQ, RQ and SQ. The highest normal form of R is
exp: Every attribute P, R, S is prime (part of some key), so all FDs satisfy the 3NF condition. R → S and S → P have non-superkey determinants, so BCNF fails.

q: Which SQL command is used to undo all changes made by the current transaction since its last commit?
exp: ROLLBACK is the TCL command that aborts the transaction and restores the last committed state.

q: Schedule S: r1(X) w2(X) r2(Y) w1(Y). Which statement is correct?
options: S is conflict serializable as T1 then T2
S is conflict serializable as T2 then T1
exp: r1(X) before w2(X) gives T1 → T2; r2(Y) before w1(Y) gives T2 → T1. The precedence graph has a cycle, so it is not conflict serializable.

q:
T(x) = 5, 10, 15. What does this return?
SELECT x FROM T WHERE x > ANY (SELECT x FROM T WHERE x <= 10);
exp: The subquery returns {5, 10}. x > ANY means greater than at least one value, i.e. greater than 5: so 10 and 15 qualify.

q: A(id) = {1,2,3} and B(id) = {2,3,4}. How many rows does SELECT * FROM A RIGHT JOIN B ON A.id = B.id return?
exp: A RIGHT JOIN keeps every row of B: ids 2 and 3 match; id 4 appears with NULLs for A. Total 3 rows (id 1 of A is dropped).

q: In a star schema, the central table is the
options: lookup table that stores only text descriptions
fact table, surrounded by dimension tables
exp: A star schema has a central fact table of measures and foreign keys linked to surrounding dimension tables.

q: Which protocol makes a distributed transaction either commit at all participating sites or abort at all of them?
exp: Two-phase commit is the atomic commit protocol (voting then decision). 2PL and timestamp ordering provide serializability, wait-die is deadlock prevention.

q: In the three-schema architecture, the level that describes how data is physically stored is the
exp: The internal schema describes physical storage structures and access paths; conceptual describes the whole logical database; external describes user views.

q:
Assertion (A): An aggregate function such as SUM() cannot be used directly in a WHERE clause.
Reason (R): WHERE filters individual rows before grouping and aggregation take place.
options: Both A and R are false
A is true and R is false
A is false and R is true
Both A and R are true, and R explains A
exp: WHERE is evaluated per row before GROUP BY, so aggregates are unavailable there; HAVING is used for conditions on groups.

q: A foreign key column in a child table
options: can contain only values present in the parent key, or NULL
must be declared as the primary key of the child
exp: Referential integrity requires each non-NULL foreign key value to match an existing parent key value; NULL is allowed unless declared NOT NULL.

q: R(A, B, C) has the FD C → B and its only candidate key is AC. Which decomposition into BCNF is correct?
exp: C → B violates BCNF (C is not a superkey). Splitting into (C, B) and (A, C) is lossless since C is a key of (C, B), and (A, C) is in BCNF.

q: Account A = 100. T1 reads A, T2 reads A, T1 writes A = A + 50, then T2 writes A = A + 50 (using its own earlier read). The final value of A is 150, though two additions should give 200. This anomaly is called
exp: T2's write overwrites T1's update because both used the stale value 100; this is the lost update problem.

q: A recursive relationship in an ER model is one in which
options: an entity set participates more than once, in different roles, in the same relationship set
exp: In a recursive (unary) relationship, such as an employee supervising another employee, one entity set plays multiple roles.

q: Which of the following is NOT a property of a relation in the relational model?
options: Tuples are ordered by their insertion time
Each attribute has a name that is unique within the relation
exp: A relation is a set of tuples, so tuple order is immaterial; insertion order is not a property of a relation.

q: Given Student(sid, name, dept) and Enrolled(sid, cid), which expression gives the names of students enrolled in course 'C1'?
exp: Join Student and Enrolled on sid, select cid = 'C1', then project name. The first option fails because cid is not available after projecting name.

q: Items(id, qty) = (1,5), (2,NULL), (3,7). What does SELECT AVG(qty) FROM Items return?
exp: AVG ignores NULLs: (5 + 7) / 2 = 6, not 12/3.

q: R(A, B, C, D) has FDs A → B and B → C. What is the highest normal form of R?
exp: The only candidate key is AD (closure of AD is ABCD). Non-prime attribute B depends on A, a proper part of the key, so a partial dependency exists: R is not in 2NF and is only in 1NF.

q: R(A, B, C, D) has FDs AB → C, C → D and D → A. How many candidate keys does R have?
exp: B is in every key. AB → C → D gives all attributes; BC: C → D → A; BD: D → A. Keys: AB, BC, BD = 3.

q: A major advantage of strict two-phase locking is that
options: it removes the need for a recovery manager
it avoids cascading rollbacks because exclusive locks are held until commit or abort
exp: Holding write locks until the end means no other transaction reads uncommitted data, so cascading aborts cannot occur.

q: Which statement distinguishes a B-tree from a B+ tree?
options: A B+ tree stores no keys in internal nodes
A B-tree can store data pointers in internal nodes as well as leaves, while a B+ tree keeps them only in leaves
A B-tree is always shorter than a B+ tree
exp: In a B-tree each key appears once and may carry a data pointer at any level; in a B+ tree data pointers are only in the leaves and internal keys are copies for routing.

q: Which SQL statement adds a new column email to an existing table Student?
options: UPDATE TABLE Student ADD email VARCHAR(50);
INSERT INTO Student ADD email VARCHAR(50);
ALTER TABLE Student ADD email VARCHAR(50);
exp: Structure changes use the DDL command ALTER TABLE ... ADD. UPDATE and INSERT change rows, not table structure, and MODIFY TABLE is not standard SQL.

q: In relational algebra, the rename operator is written
exp: ρ renames a relation or its attributes; σ selects rows, π projects columns, ⋈ is join.

q: Predicting whether a loan applicant will default (yes/no) using past labeled records is an example of
exp: Assigning an item to one of predefined classes using labeled training data is classification.

q: Which language is used to define the structure (schema) of a database, such as creating and altering tables?
exp: Data Definition Language (CREATE, ALTER, DROP) defines schema; DML manipulates data.

q: In an ER diagram, an identifying relationship (between a weak entity and its owner) is represented by
exp: A weak entity set is drawn with a double rectangle and its identifying relationship with a double diamond.

q: R(id, v) = (1,a), (2,b), (2,c) and S(id, w) = (2,x), (2,y), (3,z). How many rows does R INNER JOIN S ON R.id = S.id return?
exp: Only id = 2 matches: 2 rows in R times 2 rows in S = 4.

q: Which SQL constraint can enforce that a column 'age' must always be greater than 0?
exp: CHECK (age > 0) restricts the values that may be stored in the column.

q: Fourth normal form (4NF) is concerned with the elimination of
exp: 4NF extends BCNF by removing non-trivial multivalued dependencies whose determinant is not a superkey.

q: In two-phase locking, the lock point of a transaction is
options: the instant at which it commits
the instant at which it releases its first lock after commit
the instant at which it obtains its last lock, ending the growing phase
the instant at which it requests its first lock
exp: The lock point separates the growing and shrinking phases; the equivalent serial order of 2PL transactions follows their lock points.

q: R has 6 tuples, S has 4 tuples and R and S are union-compatible with 2 tuples in common. How many tuples does R ∪ S have?
For R(A, B, C), which expression is invalid?
exp: After π_A(R) only attribute A remains, so a selection on B cannot be applied.

q: Acc(id, bal) = (1,100), (2,200), (3,300). After UPDATE Acc SET bal = bal * 2 WHERE bal > 150; what does SELECT SUM(bal) FROM Acc return?
exp: Rows 2 and 3 are doubled to 400 and 600; row 1 stays 100. Sum = 100 + 400 + 600 = 1100.

q: A relation is in 3NF if for every non-trivial FD X → A, either X is a superkey or
options: A is a subset of X only
exp: The 3NF condition is that X is a superkey or A is a prime attribute (part of some candidate key).

q: In the wait-die deadlock prevention scheme, T1 (timestamp 5) requests an item held by T2 (timestamp 10). What happens?
options: T1 waits, because it is older
T1 is aborted, because it is older
T2 is aborted and T1 proceeds immediately
exp: In wait-die an older requester waits for a younger holder; a younger requester would die (be rolled back).

q: Log: <T1 start>, <T1, A, 10, 20>, <T1 commit>, <T2 start>, <T2, B, 5, 8>. The system crashes now. During recovery
options: both T1 and T2 are redone
both T1 and T2 are undone
T1 is undone and T2 is redone
T1 is redone and T2 is undone
exp: T1 committed before the crash so its update is redone; T2 has no commit record, so its update is undone.

q: A file has 10,000 records and a block holds 50 records. A sparse primary index has one entry per data block. How many index entries are needed?
exp: Number of blocks = 10000 / 50 = 200, so a sparse index has 200 entries (a dense index would need 10,000).
